title: inference-task-tickets-land-in-the-logs-tree
intention: The inference domain's task tickets (one JSON per inference call) land under the logs tree at address.log_path('inference_domain', 0)/tickets, i.e. ~/.cairn/logs/inference_domain/0/tickets/, instead of the device's state directory ~/.cairn/devices/inference_domain/0/tickets/; domain.tickets_dir() answers the new address (still following set_diagnostic_roots), the tickets already written move there once, and read_task_tickets and the completeness probe read them from there.
why: Akien answered open-5ec505c169c1: inference task tickets are logging artifacts and belong in the logs tree (30-day trail for relearning and forensics); today they sit in the device's state directory, grow ~280/day, and push every proof sandbox past its 150MB bound, so the tester component stays red.
traces_to: Law 5 (the address carries what a mind needs now; a logging artifact is not the device's state); Law 6 (logs/ is one machine-scoped root, so the 30-day deletion crosses nobody's gate); ticket 1c4ae8f053fe (the per-proof sandbox bound); the three retention classes (test runs and logging: 30 days, disposable).
how: Akien, verbatim (open-5ec505c169c1): 'they are a logging artifact, so the intention is that they wind up in the logging tree. their consumers are: learning loops. if we make a change to our learning, we don't have to rerun the inference calls, we can relearn off the same data. second, if we discover an issue, we have the complete history of inference for the last 30 days, a complete log trail for each call. Forensic levels of information ... It's already worked 3 times in that role.' Measured 2026-10-02: ~/.cairn/devices/inference_domain/0/tickets holds 2048 files, 73MB (1386 files, 49MB on 2026-10-01), oldest 2026-09-17; test_isolation reds at 182MB against ticket 1c4ae8f053fe's 150MB per-proof sandbox bound, and this folder is the largest grower. Every reader goes through domain.tickets_dir (cairn/devices/inference_domain/domain.py:222): _ticket_path, read_task_tickets, the probe are_inference_task_tickets_complete. address.log_path (cairn/tools/base/address.py:148) is the logs-tree address, whose why is retention ('easy to delete everything in the logs tree over 30 days old in one go', Akien 2026-08-18), and snapshot_instance_space already empties the instance root's logs/ (cairn/devices/tester/isolation.py:273-281). So: tickets_dir returns address.log_path('inference_domain', 0, table) / TICKETS; the existing files are moved once with the build (mv, not copy: a ticket has one address); the probe's docstring names the new address; long-running devices that import the domain are restarted so no stale process writes to the old address. The 30-day sweep of the logs tree itself is not this ticket's: no sweep exists in code (measured: no mtime-age deletion anywhere under cairn/), and it is cast as its own ticket.
falsifier: RED if: (1) domain.tickets_dir() with no roots table does not equal address.log_path('inference_domain', 0) / 'tickets', or it lies under address.instance_path('inference_domain', 0); (2) under a temp roots table, a ticket written through domain._write_task_ticket does not land under that table's logs tree, or read_task_tickets with that table does not read it back; (3) the live ~/.cairn/devices/inference_domain/0/tickets holds any .json file; (4) the live logs-tree tickets folder holds no ticket (the existing tickets were deleted, not moved). WRONG INTENT if a consumer needs a task ticket kept past 30 days. Horizon: the tester seal of cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_task_tickets_land_in_the_logs_tree.py.
watchme: none, because the sandbox bound in cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_isolation.py reds if anything heavy grows outside logs/ again, and tooth 3 of this ticket's proof reads the live old address at every reseal
children: none, because the 30-day sweep of the logs tree is a sibling cast as its own ticket, not a part of this move
builder_notes: A Haiku builder would ask: (1) Where? cairn/devices/inference_domain/domain.py:222, tickets_dir returns address.log_path('inference_domain', 0, table) / TICKETS; docstring names the logs tree and why. (2) The existing files? mkdir -p ~/.cairn/logs/inference_domain/0/tickets and mv the old folder's *.json there, then rmdir the old folder. (3) Proof? cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_task_tickets_land_in_the_logs_tree.py, PROVES keys 1-4, red first.

chart_claim.filled_by: CC chart chain (orient ea54e0730230 .. validate 4b7697d27ab1, each learned)

decisions.text: D1 ADDRESS: in cairn/devices/inference_domain/domain.py, tickets_dir(roots) returns address.log_path('inference_domain', 0, table) / TICKETS, where table is the same `roots if roots is not None else getattr(_trail, '_diagnostic_roots', None)` it computes today. Its docstring says the tickets are a LOGGING artifact (Akien, open-5ec505c169c1: learning loops relearn off them, forensics read the 30-day trail), so they live under <instance>/logs/inference_domain/0/tickets, the tree one 30-day deletion sweeps and every proof sandbox empties. Nothing else in domain.py changes.

D2 THE PROBE: the docstring of cairn/devices/inference_domain/probes/are_inference_task_tickets_complete.py names the address as ``logs/inference_domain/0/tickets/`` (in the logs tree, ticket 07f415c15970) instead of ``devices/inference_domain/0/tickets/``. The probe's code reads through domain.read_task_tickets and is unchanged.

D3 THE SIBLING PROOF: in cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_task_ticket.py, _tickets(tmp) reads tmp / 'logs' / 'inference_domain' / '0' / 'tickets'. Its docstring line 'the live tickets folder' stays true. No other line changes.

D4 THE MOVE, once, after the build commit: stop the ground loop (`systemctl --user stop cairn-ground-loop.service`, the transient unit holding pid 126256, measured as the writer of 827 of the 2048 tickets); mkdir -p ~/.cairn/logs/inference_domain/0/tickets; mv every ~/.cairn/devices/inference_domain/0/tickets/*.json into it (find -maxdepth 1 -name '*.json' -exec mv -n -t ... {} +, so a same-named file is never overwritten); rmdir the old folder; start the ground loop again the way the system starts it (`bin/cairn` lazy-inits it, I-the-command-lazy-inits-the-system.md), then confirm the old folder stays absent across one beat.

D5 PROOF: cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_task_tickets_land_in_the_logs_tree.py, PROVES keys 1-4 as committed red at the cast (0/4). It touches no tester code (RULE 1): clause 1 pins the address under logs/, which is all the sandbox needs.

D4 RESTART, exact: after moving the files, the loop is started by the same call every shim makes, never by hand-spelled systemd-run: PYTHONPATH=. python3 -c 'from datetime import datetime; from cairn.tools.base.shim import ensure_ground_loop; print(ensure_ground_loop(datetime.now().astimezone()))' — repeated until it prints spawned 'unit' (it spawns nothing while liveness still reads LIVE, i.e. until the stopped loop's liveness record goes stale). Observe: systemctl --user is-active cairn-ground-loop.service prints active, and after 120 s (two 60 s beats) ~/.cairn/devices/inference_domain/0/tickets still holds no .json (tooth 3 run again).

D5 THE PROOF ALREADY STANDS and is not written by the builder: cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_task_tickets_land_in_the_logs_tree.py was committed red (0/4) at the cast (commit '07f415c15970: red tooth'). Its four teeth are, in order: tickets_dir() == address.log_path('inference_domain', 0) / 'tickets' and not under instance_path('inference_domain', 0); domain._write_task_ticket under {**address.ROOTS, 'instance': tmp} lands in tmp/logs/inference_domain/0/tickets, nothing appears under tmp/devices, and read_task_tickets(roots=table) reads it back; the live old folder holds no *.json; the live new folder holds at least one. The builder runs it after D1-D4 and expects 4 passed.
